Description.Summary: IBM watsonx Orchestrate is an enterprise AI workflow orchestration platform that enables organizations to build, deploy, and manage AI agents automating business processes across domains such as HR, IT, and finance. It provides an open-source Agent Development Kit (ADK) of CLI utilities and Python modules for creating, testing, and deploying custom agents and tools.

evidence.quote: The Agent Development Kit (ADK) is a comprehensive set of CLI utilities and Python modules that enables you to create, test, and deploy agents and tools for watsonx Orchestrate.

Practices.Summary: The ADK team uses Hatch as the build and test runner. Developers run the test suite with 'hatch run test' and check coverage with 'hatch run cov'. An automated evaluation framework using ground-truth datasets allows agents to be benchmarked, with results repeated across multiple runs to assess robustness. Vulnerability (red-team) testing is also practiced to uncover weaknesses in agent policies.

evidence.quote: Run tests: hatch run test. Run coverage report: hatch run cov
The evaluate command lets you test and benchmark your agents using ground truth datasets. These datasets can be created automatically (with the generate or record commands) or prepared manually.
Evaluations can be repeated multiple times to assess performance robustness. This is configured by setting the n_runs parameter in the YAML configuration file.

Tools.Summary: Hatch is used for building and running tests in the ADK. The ADK's own evaluation framework (orchestrate evaluations) benchmarks agent behavior using ground-truth datasets and Langfuse for observability. Red-teaming is conducted via the 'orchestrate evaluations red-teaming' command group. Tool call arguments are automatically normalized during evaluation to reduce false negatives.

evidence.quote: Install dev dependencies: pip install -e '.[dev]'

Tool call arguments are automatically normalized during evaluation. This ensures that minor differences in formatting — such as capitalization, key order, value types, or list order — no longer result in mismatches.
The evaluate command supports evaluation with Langfuse.
The orchestrate evaluations red-teaming command group provides tools to list attacks, plan scenarios, and run evaluations.

Stakeholders.Summary: 61 contributors participate in the ADK repository. Vulnerability testing is documented as a critical step for AI engineers and security practitioners working with the platform.

Others.Summary: The evaluation framework records metrics including Tool Call Precision, Tool Call Recall, Journey Success Rate, Text Match Score, and Average Response Time. Red-team attacks are aligned with OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (2025): LLM01 Prompt Injection, LLM06 Excessive Agency, LLM07 System Prompt Leakage, LLM09 Misinformation.

Practices.Summary: The watsonx Orchestrate team documents a GitOps-inspired deployment strategy for agents, flows, and tools using standard CI/CD tools such as Jenkins, GitLab CI, or GitHub Actions together with the wxO CLI. The platform maintains a CI/CD-neutral stance, providing CLI tools and APIs that customers adopt into their own pipelines. A two-tenant architecture (non-production and production) with branch-based promotion is recommended.

evidence.quote: This document proposes a GitOps-inspired deployment strategy for watsonx Orchestrate (wxO) agents, flows, and tools that works without Kubernetes or Argo CD access. The approach uses standard CI/CD tools such as Jenkins, GitLab CI, or GitHub Actions together with the wxO CLI.

watsonx Orchestrate maintains a CI/CD-neutral stance, providing CLI tools and APIs that enable customers to adopt agent lifecycle management into their own existing CI/CD pipelines, regardless of the specific tools or practices they use

Tools.Summary: The ADK is distributed via PyPI as 'ibm-watsonx-orchestrate' and supports deployment to IBM Cloud, AWS, AWS Gov, and on-premises environments. The build system is Hatch. Issues.Issue_Title: orchestrate --version command returns wrong version
Issues.Description: The orchestrate --version command might not work or return the wrong version due to conflicting Python environments. Workaround is to run 'which orchestrate' and ensure it points to the correct virtual environment.

Issues.Issue_Title: Tool import permission error after Developer Edition upgrade
Issues.Description: After upgrading watsonx Orchestrate Developer Edition, importing a tool triggers permission issues. Running 'docker volume rm docker_tools-runtime-data' triggers a clean reinstall.

Issues.Issue_Title: MCP tool upload requires zip instead of folder path
Issues.Description: When uploading MCP tools from the filesystem, users must zip the tool folder. Pointing to the root folder directly is not working as expected.

Issues.Issue_Title: Tool renaming not propagated back to MCP
Issues.Description: When a tool name is modified within watsonx Orchestrate, the change is not propagated back to MCP. Tool updates are unidirectional, flowing only from MCP to watsonx Orchestrate.

Issues.Issue_Title: Agentic workflow tool fails after OpenAPI tool re-import
Issues.Description: If you delete an OpenAPI tool from the CLI and re-import the same tool, the agentic workflow tool fails because the re-imported tool gets a different tool ID and no longer matches the original reference.

Issues.Issue_Title: Tools running prematurely before all inputs are provided
Issues.Description: Depending on the LLM in use, tools might start running before all required inputs are provided. The recommended workaround is to try a different LLM.

Issues.Issue_Title: First interaction with an agent might fail to call a tool
Issues.Description: The first message sent to the agent in Developer Edition may fail due to insufficient startup time or pod failure. Workaround is to wait a couple of minutes and retry.

Issues.Issue_Title: Agent returns an empty message ('None') instead of tool calls
Issues.Description: In certain scenarios the LLM responds with 'None' instead of making tool calls. Switching the agent's style to 'default' is the recommended workaround.

Issues.Issue_Title: Agent makes multiple calls for the same tool after every message
Issues.Description: The agent might run the same tool multiple times per interaction. Providing explicit instructions in the agent definition to run the tool only once, or switching the model, resolves the issue.

Issues.Issue_Title: Agent ignores valid tools and returns incomplete responses
Issues.Description: Agents occasionally return incomplete responses with invalid tool calls when the agent recognizes the tool's response as invalid. Defining the tool as YAML with a clearer description mitigates the issue.

Issues.Issue_Title: Inconsistent transfer between multi-agent collaborators
Issues.Description: Agent-to-agent communication in multi-agent collaboration may fail due to improper instruction formatting or invalid responses. Explicit transfer instructions in the agent definition are required.

Issues.Issue_Title: Async OpenAPI tools cannot access auto-detected local IP
Issues.Description: In Developer Edition, external async tools can't access the auto-detected local IP since it isn't publicly reachable. Setting CALLBACK_HOST_URL to a public endpoint (e.g., via ngrok) enables callbacks.

Issues.Issue_Title: Tool call not working for watsonx/mistralai/pixtral-12b model
Issues.Description: Tool invocation does not function when the pixtral-12b model is used via the watsonx provider.

Issues.Issue_Title: Gemini models return UNEXPECTED_TOOL_CALL error during tool invocation
Issues.Description: Gemini models occasionally fail when invoking a tool, returning an UNEXPECTED_TOOL_CALL error. A temporary workaround is to retry the request.

Issues.Issue_Title: LLaMA models convert array of strings argument to single string
Issues.Description: LLaMA models accept only a single string as an argument. If passed an array of strings, they convert it into a single string, which may lead to incorrect results when calling a tool that expects an array.

Issues.Issue_Title: Python tools hit 2-minute request timeout
Issues.Description: Python tools use a 2-minute request timeout including environment startup. Requests to external services taking more than about 90 seconds will hit the timeout. OpenAPI tools are recommended for long-running operations.

Issues.Issue_Title: Voice-configs import failure in on-premises environments (v2.7.0 fix)
Issues.Description: Importing voice configurations failed in on-premises environments. Fixed in v2.7.0.

Issues.Issue_Title: Webchat embed command failed for deployed agents (v2.2.0 fix)
Issues.Description: The webchat embed command failed for deployed agents. Fixed in v2.2.0.

Issues.Issue_Title: Deleting an agent also deleted attached modular knowledge (v2.0.0 fix)
Issues.Description: Deleting an agent also deleted the modular knowledge attached to it. Fixed in v2.0.0.

Issues.Issue_Title: OpenAPI specs with circular jsonref objects could not be imported (v2.3.0 fix)
Issues.Description: OpenAPI specs containing circular jsonref objects could not be imported into the ADK. Fixed in v2.3.0.

Issues.Issue_Title: Agent did not respond when running a flow tool through orchestrate chat ask (v2.4.0 fix)
Issues.Description: An agent did not respond when running a flow tool through the orchestrate chat ask command. Fixed in v2.4.0.

Practices.Summary: Bug tracking for the ADK is handled through IBM Support for enterprise customers, with known issues and workarounds documented in a dedicated Known Issues and Limitations page on the developer portal. Release notes use a structured format with separate Bug Fixes sections (🐛). Common patterns across issues include LLM model-specific tool call failures, Docker-level permission errors after upgrades, and tool ID consistency problems during re-import workflows. Workarounds are documented inline until permanent fixes are released.

evidence.quote: See the known issues and limitations, and learn how to circumvent them until they get fixed
Customers of watsonx Orchestrate can raise issues with the ADK or the Developer Edition server to IBM Support

Others.Summary: A recurring pattern in issues is LLM-dependent non-deterministic behavior: tool calls fail, run prematurely, or repeat depending on the underlying model. The recommended mitigation strategy is model switching. Docker volume conflicts are another recurring class after upgrades. Timeout constraints (2 minutes for Python tools) represent a documented architectural limitation.

evidence.quote: Depending on the LLM you use, tools might start running before you provide all required inputs. To solve this, try a different LLM in your agent.

Practices.Summary: The ADK follows an approximately bi-weekly release cadence with structured versioning. Semantic versioning is used: MAJOR for breaking changes, MINOR for backward-compatible features, PATCH for bug fixes. The CI/CD tutorial documents a GitOps-inspired branching strategy with branch-based environment promotion (feature → develop → qa → staging → main). Documentation is versioned per ADK release starting from v2.0.0.

evidence.quote: Git tags mark releases using semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). MAJOR: breaking changes in I/O or behavior. MINOR: backward-compatible features. PATCH: bug fixes.
